# Prospective wrapper conformance integration

This describes a constructed-data implementation under review. It is not a
registration, target-access authorization, new experimental result or replacement
scientific protocol. The preceding producer checkpoint and its passing and failing
engineering evidence remain preserved. No original MPEA performance data or real
allocation was used to implement these changes.

The original protocol and implementation contract remain byte-identical. The
parser, mathematical study kernel, generic pool kernel, stores, feature reader,
supervisor and public aggregate projector are unchanged. Wrapper evidence is
expanded to satisfy the literal contract. New identity metadata changes receipt
digests; equivalence with the prior implementation is assessed on exact numerical
values, original memberships, orders, decisions and measurements, separately from
new-schema reproducibility.

## Closed artifacts and gates

`mpea_archive_profiles.py` defines closed feature, target and predictor descriptors.
Its framing constructor records caller-supplied observations, so the custodian
invokes it only after source size/MD5/SHA, exact complete header, every row width and
row count, and authorized-role parsing succeed. Input freeze binds the original
1,545 routes, 314 selected records, actual feature profile and the pinned header,
mapping, metadata and feature-evidence identities. Fixtures use explicitly
constructed identities and retain the unchanged actual-source rejection.

`mpea_archive_artifacts.py` projects the required development, rank, secondary
membership, completeness and calibration views from original compact evidence.
The compact compatibility members have fixed keys and are compared canonically
against the required views. No extension dictionary or alternate predictor is
introduced. Each stored target row has a separate closed provenance view retaining
its original ordinal/ID/source/role and, for both endpoints, source column, unit,
whole source identity, fixed parser identity, status/reason/exact-or-null value,
`NOT_INTERPRETED` uncertainty and `CO_RECORDED_NOT_SPECIMEN_VERIFIED` pairing.

The private `development-targets.json` is sealed before the development checkpoint.
It is reopened and validated before fitting. Both reserved vaults bind framing,
profile and row provenance. `secondary-membership.json` preserves all 40 source
groups and all 23 literal order restrictions, including empty panels.
`completeness.json` has exactly the nine declared aggregate payload members and
contains no record identities or target values. These companions are verified
before calibration and on final publication, not merely when written.

`rank-summary.json` is an aggregate companion: exact rank scientific seal,
condition-row and source-group counts, full-order count, fallback counts and fixed
scope only. It contains no threshold, IDs, predictions, neighbors or orders. The
wrapper calculates the prospective *whole stage scientific preimage*, writes this
companion, then commits the rank stage and requires its actual scientific seal to
match. The companion is not an input to the stage it references; that avoids a
cycle. Its exact expected payload and persisted bytes are verified before reserved
decoding and during final evidence-graph verification.

`mpea_archive_decisions.py` projects every scalar/tuple field directly from the
original typed generic `PoolDecision`. Full calibration and future-panel objects
remain in named shared tables and the decision contains their exact digest links.
The compact decision view is retained only as a checked compatibility view. A
source-free validator checks all views and reconstructs the generic identity
preimage; it never recalibrates or selects a second pool. Objective and constraint
references bind source SHA, columns, units, parser SHA and rank scientific seal;
the generic outcome reference additionally binds the calibration-vault scientific
seal. Evaluation-vault custody remains separately bound.

The shared flow adds only an evidence gate before fitting, an original-object
projection callback at calibration sealing and a semantic reference callback. Its
numerical algorithms and access order remain unchanged. Genuine closed-code
`StudyError` instances from the unchanged kernel are mapped by exact class and
closed argument vocabulary; unrelated exception text is never echoed.

## Resources, access and identity

Every stage has an explicitly labeled observer window from stage entry through
its pre-publication boundary, excluding its own publication and marker ACK.
Input observation begins before feature validation. Wall/process CPU are exact
fractions of integer clock differences. RSS fields are boundary observations and
process-lifetime high-water marks; within-stage peak is null/`NOT_MEASURED`, and
descendants are excluded. The unchanged supervisor separately enforces cumulative
target-phase wall time and sampled process-tree RSS with its documented limits.
Measurement failure produces explicit unavailable values, never fabricated zeros.

Original allocation publication receives usage through a narrow delegated store
view. Reproduction imports the original allocation and route bytes unchanged;
its separate import observation is attached to the new input-stage usage. This
does not rewrite the original allocation resource history.

Stage access records name actor/stage, target-custodian counter scope, authorized
columns and cumulative completed role-bundle accumulation/decoding/interpretation
counts. A role whose authorized phase may have begun without a completed counter
is unknown, not zero. Mixed source capture counts/bytes remain distinct. These
worker counters do not claim that the parent never decodes private receipts: the
parent explicitly performs a post-terminal persisted-evidence audit.

Full companion byte/content/scientific triples belong in declared envelope inputs;
scientific payload references use semantic seals. Usage is outside the scientific
preimage. This preserves exact full-byte custody without propagating observer
values through downstream scientific identities.

## Launch and reproduction audit

The registered worker still runs only after authenticated source/engineering/CI/
public-registration checks, under the existing namespace and cumulative supervisor.
Successful terminal markers are necessary but insufficient: the parent captures
and verifies all persisted stage envelopes, their predecessor links and required
companions, followed by the closed public transport and its two seals. It does not
refit, recalibrate or read the source CSV.

`mpea_archive_operations.py` is a pure helper. The caller supplies authenticated,
complete reached-stage artifact maps. The launch report separately records each
original/reproduction byte, content and scientific identity, complete-file
differences and scientific equality. Timing-related whole-file differences are
permitted; scientific mismatch clears any scientific verdict. An equal partial
map alone does not establish complete-study reproduction.

The launch report retains the bound internal supervisor receipt/status/reason and
adds the operational amendment's closed outer study status/reason. A successful
supervisor run denotes completed execution, not scientific usefulness. Unknown
failures map to `INTERNAL_FAILURE`; marker failures map to the declared stage-order
reason, without invented source or memory diagnoses.

## Verification scope

Required checks include pure closed-shape tests; private companion corruption
before dependent access and publication; exact row provenance and original
decision joins; an actual source-shaped constructed full flow under the real
supervisor; fresh-process fixed-allocation reproduction; exact numerical
comparison with the preserved baseline; and new-schema scientific equality under
different resource observations. Each review must bind its actual source bytes.
Passing earlier producer tests does not substitute for these new checks.

## Companion observability completion (prospective v3)

All seven persisted companions have closed actor/stage/column/count views. The
source-free label routes are written through the allocation observation wrapper
before its allocation seal; their cumulative pre-target counts are zero. Target
companions identify the completed authorized-role parse snapshot and its row-bundle
unit separately from cumulative mixed-source captures and bytes. Those capture
values come from the actual custodian; successful gates require one capture with
the sealed source size. The rank-summary projector's zeros describe local
projection work, not the cumulative model's prior development access.

Each companion carries the closed `companion_usage.v1` descriptor naming its
enclosing observed stage. Its own wall/CPU/peak fields are null and explicitly
NOT_SEPARATELY_MEASURED. Construction and publication fall within that stage's
observation window, but the descriptor does not assert that a later measurement
or seal succeeds. Resource failure remains unknown. No cyclic later-stage seal
is inserted into the companion. Usage remains outside the scientific preimage;
access semantics remain inside it.

Original allocation and label-route bytes are imported unchanged on reproduction;
the new attempt separately records the import observation. Exact companion
metadata is checked before target/model/consumer access, final projection and
the parent's captured-graph audit. V2's 31-test success is retained as historical
evidence. V3 uses focused common-envelope controls and independent quantitative
reproduction; root's final main suite reruns the unchanged full author paths.
